angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,426,934 km at 182.19 pc = 0.10 mas. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of the fit's two radii; no interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4889 +/- 0.0237 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 182.19 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: MASCARA-1 is a rapid rotator. Hooton et al. (2022), A&A 658, A75 fit the CHEOPS and Spitzer transits of MASCARA-1 b with a gravity-darkened oblate star: equatorial radius 2.082 solar radii and a polar radius 4.39% smaller (Table 5), so a polar radius of 1.9906. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, (2.082^2 x 1.9906)^(1/3) = 2.0511 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202141645); the scene draws the flattening, with the equatorial radius on the outline. Mass 1.9 +/- 0.063 solar masses from Hooton et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of MASCARA-1 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 7490 +/- 150 K from Hooton et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of MASCARA-1 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis, the spin axis measured against MASCARA-1 b's orbit, is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hooton et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of MASCARA-1 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass 1.9 and the radius 2.082 solar radii of Hooton et al. 2022, the sphere the limb law was read for, log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.080, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of MASCARA-1 (pscomppars): spectral type A8, from Talens et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...606A..73T/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 201585: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of MASCARA-1 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.15 dex, from Hooton et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of MASCARA-1 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.08279, from Hooton et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of MASCARA-1 (pscomppars): age 0.8 Gyr, from Hooton et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of MASCARA-1 (pscomppars): rotation period 0.853 d, from Hooton et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of MASCARA-1 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 101.7 km/s, from Hooton et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A..75H/abstract)

shape.qualification: A flattened sphere, the polar radius 4.39% smaller than the equatorial (Hooton et al. (2022), A&A 658, A75), colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json) and darkened by latitude from the same fit. No image of the photosphere exists.
